chunks: Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd narrated from Zur'ah, from Abu Basir, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: 'Verily, the womb is suspended from the Throne, and it will call out on the Day of Judgment: O Allah, bless the one who keeps my ties and cut off the one who severs my ties.' I asked: 'Is this [in reference to] the womb of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family)?' He replied: 'Rather, the womb of the Messenger of Allah is one of them.' And he said: 'Verily, the womb will come on the Day of Judgment like the hub of a wheel, which is the spindle. Whoever comes to it having established its ties, light will spread out for him until it enters him into Paradise; and whoever comes to it having severed its ties, it will constrict from him until it casts him into the Fire.'
ai.seo_question: How are family ties (rahim) described in relation to the Divine Throne and the Day of Judgment?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Kitab al-Zuhd* emphasizes the metaphysical reality of *silat al-rahim* (maintaining kinship) by personifying the womb as a divine entity suspended from the *Arsh* that actively intercedes on Judgment Day. The imagery of the womb appearing like a 'spindle' (*kubbah al-madar*) illustrates how consistent familial bonds generate spiritual light leading to Paradise, while severance results in constriction and expulsion into Hellfire, reinforcing the practical obligation of kinship in Shia ethics.

en.shaykh-tahir-ridha-jaffer: 12.Al-Naḍr ibn Suwayd narrated from Zurʿah, from Abū Baṣīr who said,

“I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh say, ‘Verily the womb, suspended from the [Divine] Throne, will call out on the Day of Judgment, “O Allah, keep ties with the one who kept my ties and cut off the one who severed my ties.”’ I asked, ‘Is this [in reference to] the womb [relations] of the Messenger of Allah (ṣ)?’ He replied, ‘Rather, the womb [relations] of the Messenger of Allah is one of them.’ He also said, ‘Verily the womb will come on the Day of Judgment in the form of a rotating object, which is [akin to] a spindle, so whoever comes to it having established its ties, it will spread light out for him until he enters Paradise, but whoever comes to it having severed its ties, it constricts him until it casts him into the Fire.’”
